answer: An operator's identities form one non-forkable wander: identity k must carry a whisper proving it reached the horizon signed by the previous head, and each horizon doubles the attested epochs of judged work required. A fresh wander is valid only if the old head whispers it and inherits the old length, so a new root cannot reset the count; the head signs once, so clones cannot branch. The kth identity costs 2^(k-1) attested epochs; ten cost 1,023. To match one honest agent, every clone must reach its own signed horizon; none can pool tenure.
